intent: Compare net worth across the listed occupations and identify how the separate ultra-rich annotation extends beyond the displayed scale.

requirements.question: How does the video present the required bars in this chart?
What wealth inequality does the chart make visually evident?

units.claim: All 6 required bar marks or stacked segments appear in the final chart.
accept: all 6 required data marks are visible in the final chart state
reject: omitting any required bar or stacked segment
replacing missing marks with a summary total or subtitle
units.evidence: All G0-required marks for the final chart state are visible and identifiable.

units.claim: The six named occupations range from -$4,000 for Cashier to $110,000 for Accountant, with Cashier the only negative value and Accountant the highest.
accept: Cashier is -$4,000 while the other named occupations range from $1,000 to $110,000
Cashier is the only negative occupation value
Accountant is the highest named occupation at $110,000

a statement that every named occupation is exactly zero without preserving the printed values

units.claim: The ultra-rich households are represented by a separate annotation whose net worth extends far beyond the displayed occupation scale.
accept: the far-right distribution curve rises extremely steeply and goes far above the displayed scale
an off-scale tail or callout labels the ultra-rich
the ultra-rich have wealth far beyond that of the six named occupations

wealth is evenly distributed across the population

units.evidence: The far-right area tail is the visual evidence: it rises steeply past the displayed axis and is labeled through an ultra-rich annotation. It is not a regular bar.
